standard.title: Identity shaped by language and culture
standard.description: reflect on and explain how their own and others' identity is shaped by language(s), culture(s), attitudes, beliefs and values
standard.prior_knowledge: Students entering at Y7-8 have lived experience of navigating between cultural-language communities, and have implicit awareness of how their identity is shaped by their linguistic and cultural background. They have not yet systematically examined or articulated this experience, nor analysed how cultural values and attitudes are embedded in language use.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on and explain how their own and others' identity is shaped by language, culture, attitudes, beliefs and values — including how cultural values influence language use, how identity is expressed through language choices, and how humour and intercultural experience shape understanding.

nodes.label: Cultural values reflected in language use
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain how cultural values and attitudes are reflected in language use — including job titles, terms of address, compliment deflection, and community-specific expressions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two examples of cultural values reflected in target language use and explain the cultural logic behind each.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss identity and cultural values in language use and interaction; explain communicative practices interpreted differently across cultures; examine how job titles and address conventions reflect respect; identify ways Chinese identity is expressed in own values, beliefs and language; explore humour across cultures.
wider: Analyse a specific communicative practice — for example, how compliments are deflected, or how thanks is expressed — across target language and English-speaking contexts, explaining the cultural values that underlie each convention
Compare how cultural identity is expressed through language in different target language community contexts — diaspora, homeland, regional — and discuss what the differences reveal
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding how cultural values are reflected in language use is the conceptual prerequisite for all identity reflection at this level. Entry students who treat communication as culturally neutral cannot engage meaningfully with the intercultural dimensions of this descriptor.

response_modes.reason: Cultural value analysis requires students to move from observing a language convention to explaining the cultural logic behind it. Explicit discussion with cultural context scaffolding builds this explanatory capacity.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two examples of cultural values reflected in target language use
Explains the cultural logic behind each example

nodes.label: Own identity across language communities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on how their own identity is shaped by their participation in multiple language and cultural communities, identifying specific ways each community has influenced their values and communication.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two specific ways different language or cultural communities have shaped own identity or communication style, and reflect on at least one experience of navigating between them.
nodes.typical_width: Explore how known languages influence ways of communicating; reflect on involvement in cultural practices and choices of language; examine how family origins reflect language use; compare cultural traditions across Chinese-speaking regions; reflect on past or possible experiences of living in a Chinese-speaking country.
wider: Interview a family member or community elder about their language and cultural identity — identify how their experience of navigating between communities differs from or resembles the student's own
Reflect on a specific moment of cultural identity navigation — describe the experience, identify what cultural values were in tension, and explain what was learned

response_modes.reason: Personal identity reflection is deepened through varied cultural encounter and comparison — single-context reflection produces limited insight. Varied reflective tasks across different community contexts and relationships build the richer identity understanding the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background language learner entry students have rich personal experience of navigating between language-cultural communities. Width investment here activates this lived experience as a source of genuine analytical insight — not only personal narrative but examined cultural understanding.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two ways different language or cultural communities have shaped own identity
Reflects on at least one specific experience of navigating between communities

nodes.label: Intercultural positioning and First Nations connections
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain communicative practices that may be misinterpreted across cultures, examine how First Nations Australian language connections compare with target language cultural connections, and reflect on how humour and communication style vary across cultural contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain at least one communicative practice from the target language community that may be misinterpreted in an Australian English context, and make at least one connection between First Nations Australian language-country connections and target language cultural connections.
nodes.typical_width: Explain practices perceived differently across cultures; examine First Nations Australian languages' connections to Country and compare with target language cultural connections; read target language jokes and analyse how humour is conveyed; discuss how humour is interpreted across cultures; reflect on own communication style differences across languages.
wider: Conduct a comparative analysis of humour across the target language and Australian English — identify what is shared and what is culturally specific, and explain what the comparison reveals about cultural values and assumptions
Reflect on own communication style across different cultural contexts — identify specific adjustments made and explain the cultural values that motivate each

response_modes.reason: Intercultural positioning integrates cultural value analysis (node 1) and personal identity reflection (node 2) into a broader, outward-looking synthesis. The teaching investment is in creating genuinely comparative conditions — real intercultural encounters, real examples of misinterpretation — that require students to examine both cultures rather than only their own.

success_criteria: Explains at least one communicative practice that may be misinterpreted across cultures
Makes at least one connection between First Nations Australian language-country connections and target language cultural connections
